profile.address: 2805 Diehl Road, Aurora, IL 60502, per this registry's own OSM tag. A City of Aurora legislative record (file 16-00890, November 2016) describes the associated CME Data Center site as spanning 2805 through 2905 Diehl Road at the southwest corner of Diehl and Eola Roads, consistent with this address as part of that same subdivided site.
profile.reading:
This building, addressed here at 2805 Diehl Road, Aurora, Illinois 60502, sits on the original CyrusOne data center site in Aurora, near the Kane and DuPage county line southwest of Chicago, a site whose defining fact is a 2016 transaction with CME Group, parent of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. Per contemporaneous trade press from Hedgeweek and per CyrusOne's own regulatory filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, CyrusOne agreed in March 2016 to acquire the roughly 428,000 square foot Aurora facility from CME Group, with the sale closing March 31, 2016 for approximately 130 million dollars as reported by Hedgeweek, or approximately 131.1 million dollars including transaction related costs as stated in CyrusOne's SEC filing, financed through proceeds of a CyrusOne common stock offering completed that same month. On April 1, 2016, CME Group signed a fifteen year lease for data center space in the building, and has continued operating its CME Globex electronic trading matching engine and providing colocation services to customers on site under that lease. CyrusOne also acquired approximately fifteen acres of adjacent land at the same time for future development, per the SEC filing.

The City of Aurora's own public legislative record, file number 16-00890, shows the City Council granting conditional approval on November 8, 2016 to a final plan covering the property from 2805 through 2905 Diehl Road, at the southwest corner of Diehl and Eola Roads, for a 416,200 square foot building addition to the existing CME data center, expanding the total building to 719,040 square feet including roughly 40,000 square feet of office space, together with equipment yard modifications, a 284 space parking plan, landscaping requirements, and subdivision of the property into four lots. The approval carried one condition, requiring the addition of 100 more deciduous shrubs and 100 more evergreen shrubs around the building's foundation. That 719,040 square foot gross building total, drawn directly from a city permitting record for the whole subdivided site as it stood in 2016, is a different measure from the 450,000 square feet of technical IT space that CyrusOne's own current marketing describes across its full three building CHI1 through CHI3 Aurora campus today, and the two figures are not reconciled here, since one appears to describe overall building shell across a subdivided multi lot site and the other CyrusOne's own later, narrower measure of usable technical space.

CyrusOne's current site names this three building campus CHI1, CHI2, and CHI3, and states 114 megawatts of total IT capacity and a 16 acre campus footprint across all three buildings together, without breaking either figure down by building. That same current site attributes the role of CME Group's home facility specifically to CHI2 rather than CHI1, a naming detail that does not cleanly match some earlier public descriptions of the original 2016 acquisition as a single building later expanded, so this registry does not assert with confidence which of CyrusOne's current CHI building numbers applies to this specific address beyond its documented role as part of the original CME associated site. No utility feed size, standby generation, or onsite generation figure specific to this building was found in any source reviewed, and no figure more granular than the 2016 acquisition and expansion filings above was located for this address individually.

CyrusOne, the operator, was founded in July 2000 and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired the company for approximately 15 billion dollars, continuing to invest in growth markets since, including a reported one billion dollars of cumulative capital investment in its separate San Antonio, Texas campuses by mid 2024 per the company's own materials, indicating this Aurora site sits within a company still actively expanding rather than one built once and left static.

reading.body:
This Aurora campus sits on the original site CyrusOne acquired from CME Group in March 2016, a transaction that left CME operating its Globex electronic trading platform in the building under a fifteen-year lease signed April 1, 2016. The acquisition included roughly 428,000 square feet of existing facility and fifteen acres of adjacent land for future development. CyrusOne expanded the total building to 719,040 square feet including office space by November 2016, per City of Aurora approval file 16-00890, and the site is now part of a three-building campus designated CHI1, CHI2, and CHI3.

CyrusOne publishes 114 MW of total IT capacity and 450,000 square feet of technical IT space across all three buildings without breaking the figures down individually. No utility power, standby generation, or onsite generation capacity specific to this address alone was found in any published source. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 114 MW across the full three-building campus would support roughly 2,850 racks as an assumption, though this figure cannot be assigned to this specific building.

This campus ranks 7th among the 6 Illinois facilities with published megawatt figures, a discrepancy that reflects its inclusion in the state's mapped facility count of 44 while most facilities publish no capacity specification. The state's published total is 236 MW across 6 facilities, placing CyrusOne's Aurora campus at roughly 48 percent of Illinois's disclosed data center capacity. The operator remains actively expanding, having invested an estimated one billion dollars cumulatively in its separate San Antonio campuses by mid-2024, indicating this site operates within a growing company rather than a static installation.
